correctness.rationale: The stationary transverse Bloch coordinate is the renewal transform r/(r+γ−iω), and the longitudinal component vanishes; the drift eigenvalues have negative real part and the Bloch radius is strictly below 1. Taking the local ω derivative at fixed γ and r in the polar full-rank SLD metric gives the stated rational QFI. Independent symbolic differentiation of that expression gives the stated sextic with positive derivative prefactor. For every t>=0 its ascending coefficient signs are ++++---. Descartes' rule and opposite signs at zero and infinity prove existence, simplicity and global maximality of the unique positive root. At t=0 the sextic factors as −(u−1)(u+1)^3(2u+1)^2, giving u*=1 and γ²F=1/16. Evaluating it at b=√(1+t) gives b^5(b−1)(b+1)^2, establishing strict separation above b for nonzero detuning. The derivative ratio at (1,0) gives the small-t coefficient 19/36. For v=√t tending to infinity and fixed c>0, v^(−8)P(cv,v²) tends to 1+2c²−2c⁴, with a unique simple positive root; bracketing on both sides and uniqueness give u*/v→√((1+√3)/2). Substitution into the scaled QFI gives 2√3/9. These are fixed-γ derivatives, not derivatives along the optimized reset schedule.
residual_risks: The full-rank proof assumes γ>0 and finite r>0; it does not treat the rank-changing undamped resonant point. It uses the unconditioned single-copy stationary QFI and no reset history or resource-rate objective.

value.rationale: This solves a natural resource-setting problem for frequency estimation when dephasing is calibrated: a global, one-dimensional root test for all detunings, an informative strict threshold, and a clear contrast with joint estimation on identical dynamics. The new scalar optimizer is useful independently of the standard QFI calculation and known undamped scaling constants.
residual_risks: No metrological advantage per elapsed time, reset overhead, adaptive information, or global estimation performance is established.
